build.summary:
Document shell, metadata, JSON-LD, icons, social card, static SEO files, next.config and both docs are done and were verified against the running dev server; type-check passes (exit 0). Two things you should know first: (1) I broke the shared dev server for about a minute — my first favicon.ico had RGB PNG frames, Turbopack could not decode it, and every route returned 500 until I restored the original; the shipped favicon uses RGBA frames and was validated in an isolated /dev/og segment before going in. (2) The dev server on port 3000 stopped listening at about 14:45 EST, after all my checks had passed; .next/trace shows a closed root span (a graceful shutdown), I ran no kill/stop command and did not restart it.

What was built:
- layout.tsx: Bunny Fonts links, both ionicons scripts, the emailjs import/init and the hand-written head tags are gone. Added `export const viewport` (theme colour #0a0f2c, viewport-fit cover) and refreshed `metadata` built from the content file; the placeholder Google verification value is removed. The next/font setup and the three font variables on <html> are unchanged.
- src/components/seo: `site.ts` (title, descriptions, keywords derived from portfolio.ts) and `StructuredData.tsx` (server component: WebSite + Person + ProfilePage, with the real LinkedIn and GitHub URLs).
- Images: /dev/og/card (1200x630) and /dev/og/icon (512x512, plus `?variant=favicon`) in pure HTML/CSS with one inline SVG star, screenshotted with the driver. A dependency-free `build-images.mjs` derives every shipped file and reproduces them byte-for-byte.
- manifest.json, sitemap.xml (lastmod 2026-11-10, the seven anchors), robots.txt, next.config.ts (`poweredByHeader: false`, `reactStrictMode: true`), README.md and DEPLOYMENT.md rewritten.

"Use multi agents": this session has no tool for spawning sub-agents, so I did the module directly as one of the eight parallel engineers.
verification: Type-check: `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` from the repo root, exit 0 with empty output, run three times (last run after all edits). No errors in anyone's files at that moment.

Head read-back via the driver on http://localhost:3000/dev/whitebox (eval): document.title = "Daniel Avila - Desktop Support Technician | IT Professional"; meta description = "Desktop Support Technician at STORIS, Inc. and Cyber Security student on the IT Help Desk at County College of Morris. Hardware, troubleshooting and IT support."; canonical href = https://www.danielavila.tech/; og:image = https://www.danielavila.tech/og-image.png (1200 x 630, image/png); og:site_name = "Daniel Avila Portfolio"; twitter:card = summary_large_image; theme-color = #0a0f2c; viewport = "width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover"; exactly one viewport and one theme-color tag; no google-site-verification tag; manifest link = /manifest.json.

JSON-LD: one script, JSON.parse succeeds, @context https://schema.org, @graph types [WebSite, Person, ProfilePage]. Person read back with name, jobTitle, description, url, image (https://www.danielavila.tech/daniel-avila.jpg 720x690), email, telephone +19739758687, address New Jersey / US, worksFor STORIS, Inc. and County College of Morris, alumniOf County College of Morris, hasCredential = the 3 entries with status "completed" (MOS with validFrom 2023-05, Apprentice Drafter, ISC2 CC), knowsAbout = 22 skills, knowsLanguage English/Spanish, sameAs [https://www.linkedin.com/in/danielavila2/, https://github.com/Happie04].

No icon 404s: in-page fetch returned 200 for /favicon.ico, /icon.png, /icon-192.png, /icon-512.png, /apple-touch-icon.png, /og-image.png, /manifest.json, /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt. The driver's previous `[http 404] /icon-192.png` line no longer appears.
Removed items confirmed in the rendered page: no "ionicons", "bunny" or "emailjs" in the document HTML; no external <link>; the only external script is the Vercel Analytics dev script.

Body classes take effect: computed background rgb(10, 15, 44), colour rgb(255, 244, 214), font-family Outfit; the three font variables resolve on <html>. No hydration warnings in the console after removing suppressHydrationWarning.

Image dimensions (sips): public/og-image.png 1200x630 (298,557 bytes); public/icon-512.png 512x512 (120,699); public/icon-192.png 192x192 (34,593); public/apple-touch-icon.png 180x180 (31,830); src/app/icon.png 512x512 (120,699); src/app/favicon.ico = 3 frames 48/32/16 px, RGBA PNG-encoded, 6,949 bytes. Next emits `<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico?..." sizes="48x48">`.

Images judged by opening the PNGs: three iterations of the card (outline thinned so letter counters stay open, extrusion smoothed, role line moved clear of the wordmark shadow, floor perspective reworked, bottom pills stopped wrapping) and of the icon (mark pulled inside the maskable 80% circle, checked with ?guide=1). The favicon variant stays legible as "DA" at 32 and 16 px; the full icon does not at 16 px, which is why the favicon uses the simplified variant. Final shots: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-faviojasso-Library-Application-Support-Claude-scratch-workspaces-2e78f3bf-6b09-4892-8e37-05d4f25b71e0-0f59886b-c83f-4098-9822-b751fbbcfb93-scratch-2026-11-10-cf9e80/381bbed9-222e-45b2-b07f-9df9e8e2450e/scratchpad/shots/seo/card-v3.png and /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-faviojasso-Library-Application-Support-Claude-scratch-workspaces-2e78f3bf-6b09-4892-8e37-05d4f25b71e0-0f59886b-c83f-4098-9822-b751fbbcfb93-scratch-2026-11-10-cf9e80/381bbed9-222e-45b2-b07f-9df9e8e2450e/scratchpad/shots/seo/icon-v3-guide.png (earlier drafts card-v1/v2, icon-v1/v2 are in the same folder).

Reproducibility: re-shot the three pages with the exact Chrome headless commands documented in README.md, ran `node src/app/dev/og/build-images.mjs ... --out <scratch>`, and `cmp` reported all six shipped files IDENTICAL (og-image, icon-512, icon-192, apple-touch-icon, src/app/icon.png, favicon.ico). The driver's screenshots and plain Chrome headless screenshots were also byte-identical.

favicon.ico validated before install: placed the candidate as icon.ico in a temporary src/app/dev/og/icotest segment — RGBA version returned 200, the RGB version returned 500 there (negative control) while /dev/whitebox stayed 200. Temporary segment deleted afterwards; served /favicon.ico is byte-identical to the built file.
next.config.ts: after the edit /dev/whitebox returned 200 on the first poll and the response no longer carries an X-Powered-By header.

manifest.json parses as JSON (4 icon entries, theme/background #0a0f2c); sitemap.xml parses as XML with 8 <loc> entries (root plus #about, #education, #skills, #experience, #projects, #certification, #contact), all lastmod 2026-11-10. The seven anchor ids exist in the course engineer's PlainPortfolio/CareerSection source at the time I checked.

Raw HTML by user agent (curl): with facebookexternalhit the title, description, canonical, og:*, twitter:* and icon links are inside <head>; with a default UA and with Googlebot they are streamed into <body> in dev (see known issues).

Screenshots of neighbours after the shell change: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-faviojasso-Library-Application-Support-Claude-scratch-workspaces-2e78f3bf-6b09-4892-8e37-05d4f25b71e0-0f59886b-c83f-4098-9822-b751fbbcfb93-scratch-2026-11-10-cf9e80/381bbed9-222e-45b2-b07f-9df9e8e2450e/scratchpad/shots/seo/whitebox-final.png, dev-plain.png and home-old-page.png in the same folder — whitebox and the plain harness render normally on the navy body.

NOT verified: a production build (`next build` is forbidden here), so metadata placement in <head> for the prerendered home page is unconfirmed; real link previews on LinkedIn/Facebook/X; Google Rich Results Test; installed-PWA / maskable rendering on a device; the favicon in a real browser tab (only the PNG frames were inspected); the final state of `/` after integration.
knownIssues: I took the shared dev server down for roughly one minute (about 14:35 EST). The first favicon.ico I installed had PNG frames without an alpha channel; Turbopack reported "Format error decoding Ico: The PNG is not in RGBA format!" and, because favicon.ico belongs to the root layout, every route returned 500 until I restored the original file. Other engineers may have seen 500s in that window.

The dev server on port 3000 is down as of about 14:45 EST: nothing is listening and there is no `next dev` process. .next/trace ends with the root `next-dev` span closing, which points to a graceful shutdown rather than a crash. I did not stop it and, per the rules, did not restart it. All evidence above was gathered before that.
Editing next.config.ts made Next reload its config once (about 14:38 EST). The server answered 200 on the first poll afterwards, but other engineers may have seen a brief recompile.

In dev, Next 15.5 streams metadata tags into <body> for ordinary browsers and Googlebot, and puts them in <head> only for HTML-limited bots such as facebookexternalhit. A statically prerendered production page should have them in <head>, but that is unverified here. If the home page ends up dynamically rendered, add `htmlLimitedBots: /.*/` to next.config.ts.

The favicon is no longer Daniel's blue-whale brand mark; it is now the gold "DA" on navy, matching the app icons. The whale is still in public/blue-whale.png and in content as credits.brandMark. To go back: `git checkout -- src/app/favicon.ico`.

hasCredential includes "ISC2 CC" because the content file gives it status "completed" (label "Course completed"); its description says it is a course completion. If Daniel does not hold the certification itself, exclude it (for example filter on `verified`).
alumniOf County College of Morris is emitted as the brief asked, although the content says graduation is expected Fall 2026.
The body uses Tailwind important variants (`font-body! bg-ink! text-cream!`) because of a legacy rule in globals.css — see contract gaps.

The old src/app/page.tsx is still in place until integration. With the new shell its headings fall back to a system font (Bunny Fonts removed), its contact form no longer has a global emailjs.init, and it still renders its own JSON-LD with the wrong LinkedIn/GitHub URLs, so `/` will carry two JSON-LD blocks until page.tsx is replaced.

The headless driver now logs `[requestfailed] https://va.vercel-scripts.com/v1/script.debug.js net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB` on every page. Vercel's security checkpoint is returning a 403 HTML challenge to headless Chrome from this machine (confirmed by loading the URL directly; curl gets 200). It is the dev-only Analytics debug script and unrelated to this module.
Sitemap entries with #fragments are kept because the brief asked for the anchor list; search engines treat them all as the root URL.
The social card and icons have Daniel's name, role, employers and location baked in as pixels; they must be regenerated if those change. build-images.mjs uses macOS `sips`.
The meta description is 159 characters; the Open Graph / Twitter description adds one sentence ("Explore the portfolio as a playable 3D hub world.").
README lists the per-module dev harnesses from the guide's module map; src/app/dev/engine, avatar and art did not exist yet when I checked, so that list should be re-read after integration.

LICENSE is MIT, (c) 2025 Favio Jasso, while the old README said "(c) 2025 Daniel Avila. All rights reserved." The new README states both (code MIT; portfolio content (c) Daniel Avila). The owner should confirm that split.
integrationNotes: Restart the dev server before integrating; it is not running (see known issues).
When composing src/app/page.tsx, delete the old page's own JSON-LD <script> (it has the wrong sameAs URLs). The root layout already renders <StructuredData /> for every route.
The contact form must pass the EmailJS public key itself (contactForm.publicKey in the content file); there is no global emailjs.init any more.
No ionicons scripts and no Bunny Fonts are loaded any more. Anything still using <ion-icon> or the Monda / Quicksand families will render without them.
Once globals.css loses its legacy `body { background; color; font-family }` rule, the `!` on the three body classes in layout.tsx can be dropped; it is harmless if left.
Body defaults are now navy (#0a0f2c) background with cream text. Light surfaces must set their own text colour; the plain-version harness already does and renders correctly.

Icons are declared explicitly in `metadata.icons`, so Next does not auto-link other icon files: adding app/apple-icon.png or a nested icon file will not produce a <link> unless it is also added to layout.tsx. src/app/favicon.ico is still linked automatically and listed first.

Never drop an .ico with non-RGBA PNG frames into src/app — it fails every route. Use `node src/app/dev/og/build-images.mjs card.png icon.png favicon.png` (README, "Icons and the social card"); add `--out <dir>` for a dry run.
Page titles: layout sets `title.template = "%s | Daniel Avila"`, so a route that exports `metadata.title = "X"` renders "X | Daniel Avila"; routes without a title keep the default.
Search/social copy lives in src/components/seo/site.ts and is derived from portfolio.ts. manifest.json, sitemap.xml and robots.txt are static and repeat the domain, name and colours by hand.

After the first production deploy, check view-source for the tags in <head> and run the validators listed in DEPLOYMENT.md. No Google Search Console verification code is configured; add a real one as `verification.google` in layout.tsx if needed.
contractGaps: src/app/globals.css still has the previous site's un-layered `body { background: var(--background); color: var(--foreground); font-family: 'Quicksand' }` rule. Un-layered CSS beats Tailwind's layered utilities, so plain `bg-ink text-cream font-body` on <body> had no effect (measured: white background, Quicksand). Worked around inside layout.tsx with important variants; the proper fix is to delete that rule, and the legacy `h1..h6 { font-family: 'Monda' }` rule, in globals.css.

The guide's module map gives this module no scripts folder, and the screenshot driver lives in a session scratchpad. To keep image generation reproducible from the repo I put a dependency-free script at src/app/dev/og/build-images.mjs (inside my lane; Next ignores it) and documented plain Chrome headless commands in the README instead of the driver.

The content file has no machine-readable dates or country code: the credential date is "May 2023" and the location is "New Jersey, USA". StructuredData.tsx parses these ("2023-05", region "New Jersey", country "US") and omits a field when parsing fails.
The brief asked for public/apple-touch-icon.png, and src/app/apple-icon.png is not in my file list, so the Apple icon is linked through `metadata.icons.apple` rather than Next's file convention.
blueprintDeviations: JSON-LD has a third node, ProfilePage (mainEntity -> the Person), in addition to the Person and WebSite the brief asked for. It is what makes the Person eligible for Google's profile-page treatment; remove the `profilePage` entry in StructuredData.tsx if it is not wanted.
Added `knowsLanguage` (English, Spanish) from the Languages skill group and kept those two out of `knowsAbout`.

The wordmark is our own lettering: one gold colour for "DANIEL AVILA" and an ice-blue "64" with a brand-blue extrusion, on Titan One — deliberately not multi-coloured letters. The star is a plain faceted gold star with no face. The card also has a checkerboard floor and a PRESS START pill, which the brief did not list.
The favicon uses a simplified variant ("DA" only, rounded transparent corners) rather than a downscale of the app icon, because the star-plus-monogram mark is unreadable at 16 px.

manifest.json: `orientation` changed from "portrait-primary" to "any" (a portrait lock would fight the 3D view on phones), and the icons are listed separately as "any" and "maskable" instead of the combined "any maskable".
robots.txt adds `Disallow: /dev/` (those pages 404 in production anyway).

next.config.ts has only the two suggested options; no security headers or other settings were added, and DEPLOYMENT.md no longer claims CSP or security headers, Netlify/Amplify/static-export paths, or environment variables that the old file described but the repo does not have.

review.summary:
The module is sound after six fixes, but nothing could be checked against a running Next server: port 3000 was down for the whole review and I am not allowed to start one. Type-check passes (exit 0) after all edits.

In place of the live read-back I used three stand-ins, all scratch-only:
- **Head tags:** ran the root layout's `metadata` and `viewport` through the installed Next 15.5.9 resolver and tag generators.
- **Art pages:** rendered the `/dev/og` pages to static HTML with the CSS and fonts the dev server had already compiled. This reproduced the builder's shipped `og-image.png` and `icon-512.png` byte-for-byte before I changed anything, so it is an exact substitute for the dev pages.
- **Shell:** compiled `globals.css` with the repo's Tailwind PostCSS plugin and read computed styles back in headless Chrome.

The builder's claims held up: removed tags, viewport export, metadata, real LinkedIn/GitHub URLs, image dimensions, RGBA favicon, reproducible image script, static files and docs.

What I fixed:
- **JSON-LD overclaim:** the ISC2 CC entry is a completed course, but it was emitted as a held "certificate" issued by ISC2. It is now named "ISC2 CC (course completed)" with no category; the two verified certifications are categorised "certification".
- **JSON-LD invalid property:** removed `validFrom`, which schema.org does not define for this credential type.
- **Keywords:** "STORIS, Inc." and "New Jersey, USA" were splitting into stray keywords in the comma-separated tag; now "STORIS" and "New Jersey".
- **Reduced motion:** `<html>` had unconditional smooth scrolling; it is now `motion-safe:scroll-smooth`.
- **Social card:** pixel stars were showing through and beside the lettering like specks; they now stay out of the text areas, and the wordmark sits 6 px higher so the role line clears its shadow.
- **Star halo (card and icon):** the gold glow on navy mixed to a muddy grey-brown; it is now Daniel's brand blue. I regenerated `og-image.png`, `icon-512.png`, `icon-192.png`, `apple-touch-icon.png` and `src/app/icon.png` with the repo's own script; `favicon.ico` is unchanged.

I also made `build-images.mjs` remove its temp folder and corrected one README claim about old anchors.

"Use multi agents": this session has no tool for spawning sub-agents, so I did the review directly.

layout: title pattern and role kept - PASS. Title resolves to "Daniel Avila - Desktop Support Technician | IT Professional".
layout: description reflects the content file - PASS. 160 characters, built from portfolio.ts (STORIS, Inc., Cyber Security student, County College of Morris IT Help Desk, hardware, troubleshooting).

Prove it: type-check - PASS. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` exit 0 with empty output, three runs, the last after all edits.

Prove it: read back the head from http://localhost:3000/dev/whitebox and confirm no icon 404s - FAIL as specified. The server was down throughout; replaced by Next's own resolver output and on-disk file checks, so no HTTP response was observed.
Prove it: open the generated PNGs and report dimensions - PASS. Opened the card, icon, favicon frames and masked previews; dimensions are listed above.
issuesFixed: JSON-LD overclaimed a credential: the completed ISC2 CC course was published as a held "certificate" recognised by ISC2. It is now "ISC2 CC (course completed)" with no category.
JSON-LD used `credentialCategory: "certificate"` for the two real certifications; it is now "certification", which matches their descriptions.
JSON-LD emitted `validFrom` on EducationalOccupationalCredential, a property schema.org does not define for that type. Removed, along with the month parser that only served it.
Keywords meta: "STORIS, Inc." and "New Jersey, USA" contained commas and split into stray keywords. Now "STORIS" and "New Jersey".
Reduced motion: unconditional `scroll-smooth` on <html> made plain-version anchor links animate for visitors who asked for reduced motion. Now `motion-safe:scroll-smooth`.
Social card: pixel stars were drawn through and beside the lettering and read as specks. Added text keep-out zones to the starfield.
Social card: the role line sat tight under the wordmark's shadow. Label and wordmark moved up 6 px.
Social card and app icon: the gold halo behind the star mixed with navy to a muddy grey-brown. Replaced with a shared brand-blue `StarGlow` component.

Regenerated public/og-image.png, public/icon-512.png, public/icon-192.png, public/apple-touch-icon.png and src/app/icon.png with the repo's build-images.mjs; favicon.ico came out byte-identical and was left alone.
build-images.mjs left a temp folder behind on every run. It now removes it.

README claimed the previous site's anchors all still work; only #about, #experience, #projects, #certification and #contact are old anchors. Reworded, and updated the reduced-motion and JSON-LD lines to match the code.
issuesRemaining: Nothing in this review was observed over HTTP from a running Next server: port 3000 was down throughout and I may not start one. The layout class change and the five regenerated PNGs have not been served by Next yet.

The new images were shot from the static render, not from the dev pages. The method reproduced the builder's files byte-for-byte beforehand, so re-running the README commands once the server is up should give the same bytes; I could not confirm that.
No production build was run (forbidden here), so metadata placement in <head> for the prerendered home page is still unconfirmed, as are real link previews and Google's Rich Results Test.
ISC2 CC stays in hasCredential, labelled as a completed course, because the content file marks it completed. Daniel should confirm; to drop it, filter on `verified` in StructuredData.tsx.
alumniOf County College of Morris is emitted as the brief asked, although the content says graduation is expected Fall 2026.
The MOS award date (May 2023) is no longer in the JSON-LD because the credential type has no property for it; it remains in the page text.
The canonical "/" is set in the root layout, so any future route inherits it unless it sets its own. Correct for a one-page site.
Sitemap entries with #fragments are kept because the brief asked for them; search engines treat them all as the root URL.
The body still needs the `!` variants because globals.css (not my file) carries the previous site's un-layered body rule.

Owner decisions carried over from the builder, unchanged: the favicon is now the gold DA rather than the blue-whale mark, and the README states code as MIT (LICENSE names Favio Jasso) with portfolio content copyright Daniel Avila.
integrationNotes: Restart the dev server first; it is not running. Then load any page and confirm /favicon.ico, /icon.png, /icon-192.png, /icon-512.png, /apple-touch-icon.png and /og-image.png return 200.

The builder's note on titles is only half right: `title.template` applies to nested routes, not to src/app/page.tsx. Next's resolver returns "Plain version", not "Plain version | Daniel Avila", for a title exported by the root page. Leave the home page without a title so the default applies.
When composing src/app/page.tsx, delete the old page's own JSON-LD script (it has the wrong sameAs URLs). The root layout already renders <StructuredData /> on every route.

There is no global emailjs.init, no ionicons script and no Bunny Fonts any more. The contact form must pass its own public key, and anything still using <ion-icon> or the Monda / Quicksand families will render without them.
<html> now carries `motion-safe:scroll-smooth` instead of `scroll-smooth`. Tailwind compiles it to a rule inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`; nothing else in src references the old class.
Once globals.css loses its legacy body rule, the `!` on the three body classes in layout.tsx can be dropped; it is harmless if left.

Icons are declared explicitly in `metadata.icons`, so Next does not auto-link other icon files added later; src/app/favicon.ico is still linked automatically and listed first. I confirmed this in the installed Next source.

Never put an .ico with non-RGBA PNG frames in src/app. Regenerate images with `node src/app/dev/og/build-images.mjs card.png icon.png favicon.png` (add `--out <dir>` for a dry run); the README has the screenshot commands.

If the home page ends up dynamically rendered, Next streams metadata into <body> for ordinary browsers; adding `htmlLimitedBots: /.*/` to next.config.ts would force it into <head>. Not needed for a static page.
